### Feature flags

Optional features are gated by instance-wide **feature flags** that admins can
flip at runtime (`on` / `off` / `beta` + per-flag user allowlist). The registry
in `backend/app/services/feature_service.py` is the source of truth; the
frontend mirrors it in `frontend/src/lib/features.ts`. Core member/tree CRUD is
never flagged.

**Every new optional feature (new view, importer, report, …) should ship behind
a flag.** That keeps rollout, beta testing, and the kill switch free. To add
one:

1. Register the name + default state in `feature_service.FEATURES`.
2. Gate its routers/endpoints with `Depends(require_feature("<name>"))`
   (`app/api/deps.py`) — disabled features must 404 on the API, hiding the UI
   alone is not enough.
3. Mirror the name in `frontend/src/lib/features.ts` (`ALL_FEATURES`, plus
   `VIEW_FEATURES` if it has a main-panel tab) and gate other UI entry points
   with `useFeature("<name>")` (components) or `hasFeature` (store actions).
   If a store is eagerly loaded on tree select, skip the load in
   `useTreeStore.connect` when the flag is off.
4. Add `admin.features.names.<name>` and `admin.features.descriptions.<name>`
   to every locale in `frontend/src/i18n/locales/`.

The resolved set for the current user is returned by `/api/auth/me` (and login)
as `features`; admins manage flags under `/api/admin/features` (Admin dialog →
Features tab).

### Database operations

1. Go through SQLAlchemy models — never build raw SQL strings.
2. Scope every query by `tree_id`.
3. Commit within the request; let FastAPI return the serialized model.
4. Update the model in `backend/app/models/` when changing the schema.

For a command that writes rows, records an activity-log entry, and then
publishes an SSE event / invalidates a cache key, wrap the commit in
`app.services.unit_of_work.UnitOfWork` instead of hand-sequencing
`db.commit()` and the side effects: queue the latter with `uow.after_commit(...)`.
They only run once the wrapped commit actually succeeds, so a failed
transaction can never publish an event or invalidate a cache key for a
mutation that didn't land. See `backend/app/api/routes/stories.py` and
`backend/app/api/routes/events.py` for worked examples.

### Process-wide services

`event_bus` (`backend/app/services/event_bus.py`), the presence registry
(`backend/app/services/presence_service.py`), the event loop reference
(`backend/app/core/runtime.py`), and the Redis client
(`backend/app/db/redis.py`) are process-wide, not per-request. Their
construction and teardown are owned by the FastAPI `lifespan` in
`backend/app/main.py`: on shutdown, after the Redis SSE listener task has
been cancelled and the pooled Redis client closed, it resets `event_bus` and
the presence registry to a clean state. This is deliberately a shutdown-only
step, not also a startup one — this app instance's own shutdown is what
guarantees the shared state is quiescent, so a subsequent lifespan in the
same process (e.g. a test that builds `app.main.app` more than once) starts
from a clean baseline without ever clearing state a still-running instance
might depend on.

Without `REDIS_URL` configured, both `event_bus` and the presence registry
fall back to in-memory state that only a single worker process can see;
with it set, they synchronize over Redis pub/sub (`event_bus`) and a Redis
hash (presence) so every worker observes the same events and roster. Set
`REDIS_URL` whenever `WORKERS > 1` — the app still runs without it, but
SSE events and presence stop being visible across workers.

content.text:
I scanned the root `AGENTS.md` (225 lines) against the actual repo state (workflows, cliff.toml, feature_service.py, docs/ contents). Here's what I found.

## Actually wrong (not just long) — fix regardless of trimming

**Golden Rule #1 (release process) is stale.** It says dispatching `release.yml` "commits `chore(release): vX.Y.Z` straight to `main`." That's no longer true — I checked `.github/workflows/release.yml` and it now opens a release PR, waits for `gh pr checks --watch`, then does `gh pr merge --squash`. The doc describes the old direct-push flow.

**Repository map's docs/ list is incomplete.** It names `AGENTS.md, COPILOT.md, SETUP.md, SECURITY.md, I18N_GUIDE.md` but `docs/` now also has `ACTIVITY_AUDIT.md`, `BUNDLE.md`, `FRONTEND_TRANSPORT_BOUNDARY.md`, `HARDCODED_VALUES.md`, `OPERATIONS.md` — none mentioned. Either enumerate them or drop the enumeration.

## Long/duplicative — good compaction targets

| Section | Lines | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| "New features — always-on or admin-toggleable?" | ~11 | Re-explains the FEATURES registry, states (`on`/`off`/`beta`), and the 4-step recipe — all already fully spelled out in `docs/AGENTS.md`'s "Feature flags" section (with the actual numbered steps). Root file's own header says deep conventions live there. Can shrink to 2-3 lines: when to flag + pointer. |
| Golden Rule #1 (release) | ~9 | Even once corrected, it lists implementation detail (which files get bumped, commit message format, exact GHCR tags) more suited to a runbook than an agent quick-start. Can compress to ~3 lines: "dispatch release.yml, don't do it locally, use dry_run to preview." |
| "Issue titles" domain list | ~4 | Enumerates 11 example domains (`ci, release, security, backend, gedcom, gallery, trees, sharing, auth, documents, quality`) in prose. Trim to 3-4 representative examples + "etc." |
| "PR titles & changelog" cliff.toml mapping | ~6 | Re-states the exact type→group mapping that's already commented in `cliff.toml` itself. Could shrink to "see `cliff.toml` for the type→changelog mapping" plus the one CI-lint pointer. |

## Verified as accurate, worth keeping as-is

Data-flow diagrams, store list (`useDatabaseStore`/`useMemberStore`/etc.), `TreeService`/`api.ts` reference, `get_readable_tree`/`get_writable_tree`/`require_admin` deps, `check-i18n` script, e2e env vars, and "e2e not a required check yet" (confirmed against the branch ruleset — only "Check Application Build" and "Check for Missing i18n Keys" are required).

## Estimate

Fixing the one factual error is a wash line-count-wise, but compacting the four duplicative/over-detailed sections above would take the file from **225 lines to roughly 165–175 lines — about a 20-25% reduction** — without losing anything CI actually enforces or anything not already covered in `docs/AGENTS.md`.

Want me to make these edits?

15	through an interactive visual tree. A React SPA talks to a FastAPI backend backed

101	admin-managed feature flag or always on**, and say which in the PR description.
102	Flags live in the `FEATURES` registry in
103	[`feature_service.py`](backend/app/services/feature_service.py), mirrored 1:1 in
104	[`features.ts`](frontend/src/lib/features.ts); each has a global state admins
105	control — `on`, `off` (kill switch), or `beta` (per-user allowlist). Reach for a
106	flag when a feature is a self-contained domain admins might disable, beta-test,
107	or kill (`gallery`, `stories`, `gedcom`, …); core member/tree CRUD is
108	intentionally not flaggable. The four-step recipe is at the top of
109	`feature_service.py`. **If it's unclear which way to go, ask the requester** — it
110	is hard to reverse once the UI and data model assume one.
111	
112	## PR titles & changelog
113	
114	PRs are squash-merged, so **the PR title becomes a commit subject on `main` —
115	and release notes are generated from that history**, not hand-written. There is
116	no changelog file to hand-edit; generated notes are published only to
117	[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/maxi-smidt/family-tree/releases).
118	
119	PR titles **must be a [Conventional Commit](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
120	subject** — `type(scope): summary`, e.g. `feat(gallery): add face-tag search`
121	or `fix(sharing): revoke access for open sessions`; a CI lint job
122	([`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`](.github/workflows/pr-title-lint.yml))
123	rejects PRs whose title doesn't parse. [`cliff.toml`](cliff.toml) maps types to
124	[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/) groups when a release is cut:
125	`feat` → Added, `fix` → Fixed, `perf`/`refactor` → Changed, `security` →
126	Security. `chore`, `typing`, `test`, `docs`, `ci`, `build`, and `style` are
127	internal-only and excluded from generated notes — pick one of those types for
128	work users never see instead of `feat`/`fix`.
129	
130	## Golden rules — CI enforces these; a PR fails without them
131	
132	1. **Do not bump the app version on ordinary PRs.** Cutting a release is a
133	   maintainer action, not a local step: dispatch the
134	   [`release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml) workflow (Actions tab →
135	   "Release" → Run workflow) with the version segment to bump. It bumps
136	   `frontend/package.json` + lockfile + `backend/pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`,
137	   commits `chore(release): vX.Y.Z` straight to `main`, re-runs the full check
138	   suite and E2E against that commit, publishes GHCR images tagged `X.Y.Z` and
139	   `latest`, and creates the matching GitHub Release with generated notes. Use
140	   `dry_run: true` to preview the version and notes without changing anything.
141	2. **All user-facing text goes through i18next** and must exist in every locale
142	   under `frontend/src/i18n/locales/`. Run `npm run check-i18n` (from
143	   `frontend/`); the [CI](.github/workflows/check-build.yml) workflow gates it.
144	   Keys are hierarchical: `<feature>.<component>.<element>` (see
145	   [docs/I18N_GUIDE.md](docs/I18N_GUIDE.md)).
146	3. **Both apps must build & test green.** The
147	   [CI](.github/workflows/check-build.yml) workflow runs the frontend build +
148	   Vitest and the backend ruff + compile + pytest. Match it locally before
149	   pushing (commands below).
150	
151	## Toolchain
152	
153	**Node.js 24** (frontend, npm; dev floor v20.19+/v22.12+) and **Python 3.12 +
154	[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)** (backend — not pip/poetry). Don't rely on
155	system defaults; they are usually too old.
156	
157	## Commands
158	
159	### Setup & run (development)
160	
161	Config lives in a single repo-root `.env` (copy from `.env.example`), read by
162	both docker-compose and a host-run dev backend. Full walkthrough:
163	[docs/SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md).
164	
165	```bash
166	docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d db                            # dev Postgres on :5432
167	cd backend  && uv sync && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000   # API docs at /api/docs
168	cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev                                    # :1420 (proxies /api → :8000)
169	```
170	
171	### Match CI before pushing
172	
173	```bash
174	# Frontend (from ./frontend)
175	npm run build            # tsc type-check + vite build
176	npx vitest run           # one-shot unit tests (note: `npm test` is watch mode)
177	npm run check-i18n       # translation parity
178	
179	# Backend (from ./backend)
180	uv run ruff check
181	uv run python -m compileall -q app alembic && uv run python -c "import app.main"
182	uv run pytest          # add -n auto to match CI's parallel run (pytest-xdist)
183	```
184	
185	### End-to-end tests (Playwright)
186	
187	```bash
188	docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yml up --build -d   # full stack on :8080
189	cd e2e && npm install && npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
190	E2E_ADMIN_USERNAME=e2e-admin REDACTED npx playwright test
191	docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yml down -v
192	```
193	
194	`E2E_ADMIN_*` must match the stack's `FIRST_ADMIN_*` (defaults `e2e-admin` /
195	`e2e-admin-password`); override `E2E_BASE_URL` for remote stacks. Reports land in
196	`e2e/playwright-report/`. The `e2e.yml` workflow runs on PRs to `main` but is not
197	a required check yet.
198	
199	### Database migration (after editing `backend/app/models/`)
200	
201	```bash
202	cd backend && uv run alembic revision --autogenerate -m "describe change"   # review it
203	uv run alembic upgrade head
204	```
205	
206	## Conventions (short form)
207	
208	- TypeScript **strict**; no `any` (use `unknown`). Interfaces for object shapes.
209	  Prettier owns all formatting (auto-runs on commit via husky).
210	- Components: PascalCase files; hooks `useX`; tests co-located as `*.test.ts`.
211	- Tree layout is computed in `frontend/src/utils/layoutUtils.ts` (dagre) — never
212	  set node positions manually; recompute the full layout.
213	- Full conventions, file organization, and task recipes:
214	  **[docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md)** and **[docs/COPILOT.md](docs/COPILOT.md)**.
215	  Security / export-encryption model: **[docs/SECURITY.md](docs/SECURITY.md)**.
216	
217	## PR checklist
218	
219	- [ ] Version bumped only if this is a release-preparation PR (`npm run bump:*`)
220	- [ ] `npm run build` + `npx vitest run` pass (frontend)
221	- [ ] `uv run ruff check` + `uv run pytest` pass (backend)
222	- [ ] `npm run check-i18n` passes; new strings translated in **all** locales
223	- [ ] Schema changes have an Alembic migration
224	- [ ] PR title is a Conventional Commit subject (`type(scope): summary`) — it
225	      becomes the changelog line for this change
